plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single-batch bulk RNA-seq experiment: Salmon-derived raw integer gene-level counts for 12,000 gene symbols across 12 skin samples (counts.csv, 12000 x 13 — first column gene symbol), with metadata.csv giving one condition label per sample (6 atopic dermatitis lesional vs 6 control, unpaired). The research question has two parts — which genes change, and which hallmark pathways change — plus an explicit data-quality concern: sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median.

The plan runs in three steps on one track. T1S1 handles the QC/robustness question head-on rather than deciding it by fiat: it recomputes library sizes and detected-gene counts from counts.csv, places sample_01 in a PCA / sample-correlation / RLE context, and decides whether the low depth is a benign depth effect (correctable by size-factor normalization, which is exactly what a negative-binomial method does) or a genuine outlier that also separates on expression structure. Median-of-ratios / TMM size factors absorb a 4x depth difference well; what they do not absorb is the extra dispersion and the loss of detection at low counts, so the step reports both and issues an explicit keep/drop recommendation with the evidence behind it.

T1S2 does the differential expression with a negative-binomial count model (DESeq2 preferred; edgeR quasi-likelihood or limma-voom with observation weights as installed fallbacks — the package inventory could not be read, so the step must probe before importing). Critically, it runs the same ~lesional-vs-control contrast TWICE — all 12 samples, and the 11 remaining after dropping sample_01 — and reports the concordance between them. With n=6 per group a single influential sample can carry a hit list, so the primary result is defined as the full-12 analysis and the sensitivity analysis is what qualifies it. Independent filtering of low-count genes and BH FDR are applied; no fold-change-only ranking.

T1S3 takes the ranked gene list to hallmark pathways via GSEA on the full shrunken-LFC/stat ranking (not an over-representation test on a thresholded list, which throws away the ranking and is fragile at n=6). Hallmark gene sets are NOT present in the environment — the reference store reports itself unprovisioned — so the step must first resolve them from whatever the environment holds at run time (msigdbr, a staged GMT, or gseapy's gene-set access if any is offline-capable), and if none is available it must report that plainly and fall back to a documented small set of hand-specified immune/keratinocyte gene sets, labelling those results as non-hallmark. Enrichment is also re-run on the drop-sample_01 ranking so that pathway calls inherit the same robustness check.

Limits stated up front: n=6 vs 6, unpaired, single batch, 12,000 genes only (a filtered or partial annotation, so absolute pathway coverage will be understated); no covariates beyond condition are available in metadata.csv, so age, sex, and body site are uncontrolled confounders that cannot be adjusted for here.
